punchline: Schatz plated the soil that gave streptomycin; the Nobel went to Waksman alone.
thirty_sec: Albert Schatz, a Rutgers PhD student, found the streptomycin-producing strain in his eleventh soil plating; he sued over credit in 1950 and the case settled, while the 1952 Nobel Prize went to Selman Waksman alone.
question: On your shared project, whose contribution is likeliest to be forgotten, and when will you write it down?
key_contrast: Agree on credit while everyone is still generous.
